concepts.title: SI Units: Base and Derived
concepts.definition: Every physical measurement compares the quantity against an agreed reference standard called a unit. The international system (SI) fixes seven base units -- metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela -- and all other units are built from these as derived units by multiplying and dividing powers of the base units.
concepts.key_idea: Seven base units anchor all of physics; every derived unit is just an algebraic product of powers of the base units.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph101.txt lines 10-120 (sections 1.1, 1.2; unit as reference standard, seven SI base units, table of base quantities)
question_patterns: list the seven SI base units and their physical quantities
in class 11 units and measurement: what is a derived unit
why is a standard unit needed before reporting any measurement
express the newton in terms of SI base units
which base unit measures amount of substance
is the joule a base unit or a derived unit

solution_steps.explain: Length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity carry the metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.
A derived unit such as the newton is assembled from base powers: kg m s^-2 -- no new base standard is needed.
Reporting a measurement means quoting how many times the chosen unit fits into the quantity -- a number plus a unit.

concepts.title: Dimensions of Physical Quantities
concepts.definition: The dimension of a quantity records which base quantities it is built from and to what powers, written in square brackets such as [M L T^-2] for force. Dimensional formulas let physicists classify quantities independently of any particular unit system.
concepts.key_idea: A dimensional formula is the recipe of base-quantity powers behind any derived quantity.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph101.txt lines 121-210 (section 1.4 dimensions of physical quantities, dimensional formulas, examples of force and energy)
question_patterns: write the dimensional formula of force
in class 11 units and measurement: what do the symbols M, L and T mean in dimensions
find the dimensions of kinetic energy
why are dimensionless quantities special
state the dimensions of pressure
are dimensions of work and torque the same

solution_steps.action: expand the quantity into base quantities
solution_steps.explain: Write the defining relation and replace every symbol by its composition of mass, length, time and the other base quantities.
Powers of each base quantity combine by adding exponents across products and subtracting across quotients.
The result is stated as [M^a L^b T^c ...] -- zero power on a base quantity simply drops it from the formula.

concepts.title: Dimensional Analysis: Checking and Converting
concepts.definition: Because adding unlike dimensions is meaningless, every correct physical equation must have matching dimensions on both sides -- a test dimensional analysis applies instantly. The same technique converts a quantity from one unit system to another by multiplying with ratios that equal one, and it can even suggest the form of a dependence among quantities.
concepts.key_idea: Dimensions must balance across equals signs and plus signs -- anything else cannot be physics.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph101.txt lines 211-290 (section 1.5 dimensional analysis and its applications, checking equations, unit conversion, example 1.4 and 1.5)
question_patterns: check whether the given equation is dimensionally correct
in class 11 units and measurement: convert a quantity from one system of units to another using dimensions
why can dimensions only give the form of a relation and not its constant
find the dimensions of the constant in the given formula
derive the dependence of a period on length and gravity using dimensions
can dimensional analysis detect a wrong numerical coefficient

solution_steps.explain: Replace each term of the equation with its dimensional formula.
Terms that are added or equated must share identical dimensions; a mismatch exposes an incorrect relation.
To change systems, multiply the numerical value by the ratio of old and new base units arranged to cancel correctly.

concepts.title: Volume and Density from Measured Dimensions
concepts.definition: For a rectangular sheet or block, multiplying its length, breadth and thickness gives the volume it occupies; dividing the mass of that body by the volume then yields its density. This pipeline from direct measurements to a derived quantity is the everyday work of measurement physics.
concepts.key_idea: Three ruler readings make a volume; one weighing turns it into density -- derived quantities ride on direct ones.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph101.txt lines 291-340 and exercise 1.11 (mass, length, breadth, thickness of a rectangular sheet; density idea of chapter exercises)
question_patterns: find the volume of the rectangular sheet from its length breadth and thickness
in class 11 units and measurement: compute the density of a block with given mass and dimensions
calculate the volume from the three measured dimensions
the mass and volume are given, determine the density
how many significant figures should the computed density carry
express the volume in SI units after converting the measurements

solution_steps.explain: Length, breadth and thickness multiply to give the volume of the rectangular body.
Density is mass packed into each unit of volume.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Significant Figures
concepts.definition: Significant figures are the digits in a measurement that carry meaning -- every reliably known digit plus one uncertain digit. Zeros between non-zero digits count, leading zeros do not, and trailing zeros count only when a decimal point is present; computed results keep no more significant figures than the weakest input.
concepts.key_idea: Report no more digits than your measurement earns -- the last digit is always the doubtful one.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph101.txt lines 341-430 (section 1.6 significant figures, rules for counting, exercise 1.10 examples)
question_patterns: state the number of significant figures in the given measurement
in class 11 units and measurement: which zeros in a number are significant
round the result of a calculation to the proper significant figures
why does 2.308 have four significant figures
how many significant figures survive when two measurements are multiplied
express 0.00052 in scientific notation and count its significant figures

solution_steps.explain: Rewrite the number in scientific notation so only the coefficient digits remain in view.
Leading zeros never count, trapped zeros always count, trailing zeros count with an explicit decimal.
Multiplication and division keep the smallest input count of significant figures; addition keeps the coarsest decimal place.

concepts.title: Errors in Measurement: Absolute, Relative and Combination
concepts.definition: No instrument is perfect, so every reading carries an error. The absolute error is the spread of individual readings around their mean; relative error is that spread divided by the mean value; when quantities combine, absolute errors add under addition and subtraction, while relative errors add under multiplication and division.
concepts.key_idea: Adding quantities grows absolute errors; multiplying quantities grows relative errors -- that is the whole combining rule.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph101.txt lines 431-520 (sections 1.8 accuracy precision and errors, absolute and relative error, error combination rules)
question_patterns: find the mean absolute error of the repeated readings
in class 11 units and measurement: how do errors combine when quantities are multiplied
compute the relative error in the computed density
distinguish accuracy from precision of an instrument
the period of oscillation was measured many times, report the error
what fraction of the result is the percentage error

solution_steps.explain: The mean of several readings is the best estimate of the true value.
Averaging the sizes of the departures from the mean gives the mean absolute error.
For products and quotients add the relative (percentage) errors of the factors to get the relative error of the result.
